subject: Accounting
title: Receipt Scanning and OCR
description: A fast breakdown of Receipt Scanning and OCR for builders.

hook.text: Snap a photo of a receipt. The app reads the vendor, date, and amount automatically.

buildup.text: Optical character recognition (OCR) converts images of receipts into structured financial data.

discovery.text: The data auto-fills expense entries—reducing manual typing and lost-receipt headaches.

twist.text: OCR isn't perfect—faded ink, wrinkled paper, and unusual formats still cause misreads.

climax.text: Combined with cloud storage, digital receipts create a permanent, searchable archive.

punchline.text: Snap, scan, done. Paper receipts are going extinct.

quiz.question: What does OCR technology do for bookkeeping?
options: Converts receipt images into structured financial data
Replaces the need for bank accounts

details.summary: Receipt scanning and OCR technology let bookkeepers capture expense data by photographing paper receipts. This topic covers how optical character recognition extracts key data, its accuracy limitations, and how it streamlines expense tracking.
details.whyItMatters: Lost receipts are the bane of expense tracking and tax deductions. Digital capture with OCR creates a searchable, permanent record that simplifies bookkeeping and audit preparation.
takeaways: OCR technology extracts vendor, amount, date, and tax information from receipt images
IRS accepts digital receipt copies as valid documentation for tax deductions
Modern OCR accuracy exceeds 95% but still requires human review for unusual receipts

faq.question: What is OCR in bookkeeping?
faq.answer: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) is technology that reads text from images of documents like receipts and invoices, automatically extracting data such as vendor name, amount, date, and tax—allowing bookkeepers to digitize paper records quickly.

faq.question: Does the IRS accept scanned receipts?
faq.answer: Yes. The IRS accepts digital copies of receipts as valid documentation under Revenue Procedure 98-25, provided the electronic copy is an accurate reproduction of the original. This means you can safely scan receipts and discard paper versions.
